task.title: Separate privileged task intake from genuine MFA-bound execution authorization

revision_history.summary: Independent exact-head review found 8 concrete P1 defects plus an earlier read-only source diagnostic's 4 executable false-positive observations; see required_changes_addressed below. The GitHub write of this REJECT decision itself failed (HTTP 422); canonical review/task state still recorded the reopen and moved responsibility to the owner.
This evidence revision. Addresses all 8 review findings and the 4 diagnostic false-positives with real code changes plus new regression tests; see required_changes_addressed.

required_changes_addressed.finding: supervisor.py:3170 looked up tasks via task_index_from_status(config, state) -- state is dispatch-loop runtime/queue state, not a canonical status snapshot, so the lookup was always empty and the authoritative reserve step was silently skipped for every task, including privileged ones (an isolated actual-process probe showed a launch still proceeding after revocation was injected between admission and launch).
required_changes_addressed.fix: start_worker_for_request now takes an explicit latest_task_map parameter (the already-freshly-loaded canonical snapshot process_queue computed moments earlier) and uses it only to decide whether a privileged policy exists at all (an immutable structural fact, safe from a slightly stale snapshot); when it does, reserve_execution_authorization_for_launch is always called and performs its own authoritative reload/CAS under the exclusive lock. When no latest_task_map is supplied, the authoritative reserve is always invoked instead of silently skipped.

required_changes_addressed.finding: execution_authorization.py:407-414 authorized hosted provenance with a missing execution_authorization subrecord, an empty/corrupt record, a missing policy, or requires_execution_authorization=false; supervisor.py:3100-3105 also returned successfully in these cases.
required_changes_addressed.fix: is_execution_authorized now derives ground-truth privileged classification from the task's durable dev_bridge.work_class via a new _task_privileged_by_source helper, independent of whether the execution_authorization subrecord happens to be present. A privileged task with a missing subrecord, a malformed policy, or a downgraded requires_execution_authorization flag now fails closed (returns False) instead of falling back to authorized.

required_changes_addressed.finding: scripts/ai_status.py:5570-5584 trusted a caller-supplied EXECUTION_MFA_ISSUER_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON environment variable as the MFA-issuer trust root. An isolated local Human/Ops ingress accepted a caller-generated key also labelled as source signing authority with self-asserted MFA in the same command invocation.
required_changes_addressed.fix: command_execution_grant_submit no longer reads any environment variable for the trust root. A new _trusted_execution_mfa_issuers helper sources it exclusively from execution_authorization.mfa_issuer_public_keys in the on-disk .orchestrator/config.json (added as a new, narrow, empty-by-default config section) via load_config(), which the same CLI invocation's environment cannot set. EXECUTION_GRANT_JSON (the signed assertion itself, not a trust root) is unaffected.

required_changes_addressed.finding: execution_authorization.py:420-430 did not validate the task's current contract/resources. command_execution_resource and command_artifact_contract could both change scope after a grant was issued while preserving generation and is_execution_authorized=true, because the stored policy_digest was never recomputed against the task's current fields.
required_changes_addressed.fix: execution_policy_digest and derive_execution_policy now also bind the artifact contract. is_execution_authorized recomputes the digest against the task's current target_repo/execution_resources/artifacts on every call and fails closed on any mismatch against the frozen policy_digest, so a scope revision made after grant issuance invalidates the outstanding grant even without a generation bump.

required_changes_addressed.finding: execution_authorization.py:185's old_runtime_hold was an unrecognized new field with no old-runtime-recognized meaning, and runtime_supports_execution_authorization had no production caller. A frozen-base actual dispatch predicate admitted the new hosted pending/no-grant record with completed dependencies.
required_changes_addressed.fix: Two independent layers. (1) A fresh privileged task now also gets the pre-existing, universally-honored waiting_for="Human/Ops" hold at intake (command_assign), which any dispatch-admission revision -- including one that predates execution_authorization.py entirely -- already refuses to dispatch; execution-grant-submit clears it once a genuine grant is bound. (2) runtime_supports_execution_authorization's boolean-value bug is fixed (a mapping now checks the capability's *value*, not merely key presence), and it gets a real production caller: scripts/promote_supervisor_runtime.py's new verify_execution_authorization_barriers discover-only-probes a candidate command runtime's own interpreter for execution_authorization.py, worker_runner.py's entry hook, and dispatch_admission.py's execution_authorized field before promotion, refusing an old-runtime rollback target that lacks any of them. It runs in the same preflight position as the existing verify_worker_sandbox check, before the healthy incumbent is ever stopped.

required_changes_addressed.finding: worker_runner.py had no canonical execution binding check before the provider Popen call, and reserved_run_id/run_ttl_seconds/revocation had no worker/recovery enforcement -- a direct invocation could launch owner-execution work without ever consulting execution_authorization.
required_changes_addressed.fix: A new execution_authorization.reservation_is_current(task, run_id, now) pure query requires a live, current, unexpired STATE_RESERVED record bound to the exact run id. worker_runner.py's new ensure_execution_authorized_before_launch calls it (for the owner role only) immediately before subprocess.Popen, reading the canonical task directly from ai-status.json. The exact bound run id is threaded from supervisor.reserve_execution_authorization_for_launch through request.metadata['execution_authorization_run_id'] -> common.delivery_runtime_env's new ORCH_EXECUTION_AUTHORIZATION_RUN_ID env var (an adapter's own new_runtime_id-generated --run-id is unrelated and cannot be used for this binding).

required_changes_addressed.finding: execution_authorization.py has a caller-holds-lock docstring but consume_grant_nonce/reserve_execution_authorization were pure in-memory helpers; the required real two-process/no-unauthorized-launch integration and tests were missing.
required_changes_addressed.fix: The imperative claim/lease integration already exists in supervisor.reserve_execution_authorization_for_launch (exclusive canonical task-state lock, load-verify-CAS-write); this revision fixes the bug (finding 1 above) that made it unreachable for a privileged task and adds the worker-entry counterpart (finding 6). Isolated reserve/CAS-race and worker-entry-TTL/state coverage is in test_execution_authorization.py; DurableQueueContractTests exercises the actual supervisor dispatch-loop integration under mocked load_status snapshots. A genuine live two-process OS-level race and a real bwrap-sandboxed worker_runner subprocess launch were not additionally exercised in this revision; see not_delivered.

required_changes_addressed.finding: rewrite/dispatch_admission.py:370 applied the execution-authorization mutation gate to REVIEW_READY and OWNED_FINALIZE dispatch reasons too, so a reserved/expired/pending privileged task could not even receive read-only review or finalization dispatch.
required_changes_addressed.fix: The EXECUTION_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED denial is now scoped to task_reason in (OWNED_IN_PROGRESS, OWNED_READY) only -- derived from the same canonical, non-spoofable dispatch_reason() computation already used for lifecycle gating, not a caller-supplied label. supervisor.start_worker_for_request's reserve call is scoped the same way via request.reason. REVIEW_READY/OWNED_FINALIZE dispatch of a privileged task is now unaffected by its authorization state, matching SA/SD 4's 'read-only review/status/finalization must not acquire a mutation permit or clear a pending gate'.

required_changes_addressed.finding: The prior evidence.json described the two-process race as sequential in-memory reserve calls and mocked-lock unit tests, not a real race; it also omitted claimed deselection arguments, described a pass_pending_commit_reverify status that was never followed up, and its embedded plan copy's source hash did not match the original.
required_changes_addressed.fix: This revision's evidence records exact commands/exits/counts (see verification below), does not claim a real OS-level two-process race was exercised (see not_delivered), and the repository-readable EXECUTION_AUTHORIZATION_SA_SD.md copy's verbatim source section is unchanged from the original signed text; only the living 'Implementation status' / 'Operational command/receipt contract' commentary around it (not the verbatim section) was updated to match this revision's actual behavior.

diagnostic_false_positives_addressed: is_execution_authorized(privileged task with no execution_authorization subrecord) now returns False (was True)
is_execution_authorized(privileged task with execution_authorization={"policy": "corrupt"}) now returns False (was True)
is_execution_authorized(privileged task with policy.requires_execution_authorization=False) now returns False (was True)

not_delivered.runtime_promotion: Source acceptance and qualified-runtime promotion (actually running verify_execution_authorization_barriers and verify_worker_sandbox against the live production command-runtime candidate, proving both barriers are live on the promoted supervisor runtime) is a separate step per plan section 6-7, performed after this PR merges through the existing qualified runtime promotion workflow, not by this task directly.
not_delivered.real_two_process_os_race: The two-process spend race is proven via an isolated in-process CAS check (a second reserve_execution_authorization call against an already-STATE_RESERVED record raises), not a real two-OS-process concurrent launch against a live TaskStore/lock file. The existing canonical_task_state_lock_file exclusive-lock machinery this reuses is not itself new or retested by this task.
not_delivered.real_bwrap_sandboxed_worker_runner_two_r: ensure_execution_authorized_before_launch's refusal path is covered by unit-level reservation_is_current tests and by the existing worker_runner.py test suite's unaffected-non-privileged-task coverage; a dedicated end-to-end subprocess test that launches worker_runner.py for a privileged task inside a real bwrap sandbox and asserts zero process/effect on refusal was not added in this revision, matching the pre-existing gap noted in test_worker_runner_heartbeat.py's own bwrap-availability-gated tests.
not_delivered.hosted_task_resubmission: Section 7's revised, signed, pending-authorization submission of DEV-RELEASE-HOSTED-001 / L12-HOSTED-001 / MGMT-AGORA-E2E-001 explicitly waits on accepted source AND qualified-runtime/no-MFA no-launch evidence; it is not performed by this task.
not_delivered.live_mfa_issuer: No live MFA issuer/proof exists yet; .orchestrator/config.json's execution_authorization.mfa_issuer_public_keys ships empty by default, so grant submission and execution remain closed with an actionable issuer-not-configured reason until one is operationally provisioned. This does not block storing pending privileged tasks.
